_note: WHAT SIZE TO DRAW IT AT IN A SCENE. The source art is NOT to scale and nothing in the atlas says so: every animal is authored on the game's 32x64 grid because in the game every entity IS a grid cell, so a cat (16x42), a hen (26x43), a bulldog (29x42), a mule (28x63) and a grown man (30x52) are within a few pixels of each other. Drawn 1:1 they are a row of identical silhouettes, which is exactly what the first title screens came out as. The buildings are on a THIRD scale again -- ranch.barn is 400px wide and ranch.windmill 128, when a windmill is taller than a barn is wide.
_reference: A GROWN PERSON IS 64 PIXELS TALL. That is 36.6px per metre, and every number below is derived from what the thing actually is at that scale. A barn is about 12m wide, so 440. A round bale is 1.5m, so 55.
_readabilityNote: Small animals sit deliberately ABOVE life scale. A cat is about 25cm at the shoulder, which would be 9px and unreadable. Readability wins over arithmetic; what matters is that the ORDER is always right -- hen < dog < pony < barn -- and tests/content.test.ts asserts exactly that.
_unitsNote: THE TWO FAMILIES ARE IN DIFFERENT UNITS and must not be compared across. A cast entry is a HEIGHT; a building or vehicle entry is a WIDTH, because that is the dimension each is naturally described by. A chicken coop is 92 here and an Arabian horse 104, and the coop is not smaller than the horse -- it is about 2.5m wide and about 2m tall, so it is wider than a horse AND shorter than one at the same time. A test that compared the two failed for exactly this reason, and the test was the thing that was wrong.
_heightNote: GENERATED by `npm run scale`. `drawAt` is a WIDTH for anything with a dotted key (buildings, vehicles, props) and a HEIGHT for the cast. `drawAtHeight` is the measured companion for the width-keyed ones, and it must be measured rather than inferred: the ranch group is packed UNTRIMMED, so the frame rect is the generation canvas and the art floats inside it. ranch.farmhouse is a 256x320 canvas holding 194x165 of house, so inferring height from the canvas made a 330-wide house 413 tall instead of 281 and put it above the barn. `contentBox` records what was measured.
_artWinsNote: This replaced a hand-written `tallOverrides` block that was derived from REAL dimensions rather than from the sprites. A real farm windmill is about 10m tall and 2.5m wide, so 100 wide implied 366 tall; the sprite is 68x115, a ratio of 1.7 and not 4, and drawing it at 366 stretched it. Where the art and the world disagree, THE ART WINS: a stretched sprite is a visible defect and a short windmill is a style choice. Wanting a taller windmill is a regeneration, not a multiplier.
